content:
Logical reasoning is the section that separates a good Class 2 Olympiad score from a great one — series, odd one out, analogies, coding and mirror images. This guide explains how to think about each type, the traps, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 2 Maths Olympiad Logical Reasoning chapter tests

  • Series — what comes next (numbers and figures)
  • Classification (odd one out)
  • Analogies (A is to B as C is to ?)
  • Coding-decoding, mirror images and spatial reasoning

Key facts your child should know

  • For a series, find the rule (a number step or a repeating shape/colour) and continue it.
  • For odd one out, find what most items share; the one that breaks the rule is the answer.
  • For an analogy, use the same link in the second pair as in the first.
  • A mirror image flips left to right.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Picking an odd-one-out when two rules seem to fit — look for the single clear rule.
  • Continuing a series by the wrong feature.
  • Flipping a mirror image top-to-bottom instead of left-to-right.

quiz.title: IMO Class 2 Logical Reasoning Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: If A = 1, B = 2, C = 3 and so on, which word do the numbers 10, 1, 13 spell?
questions.explanation: 10 = J, 1 = A, 13 = M. So the numbers spell JAM.
In the first pair each number is doubled (3 becomes 6). Doing the same to 8 gives 16.

questions.q: Arjun is standing 4th from the left in a row of 15 children. What is Arjun's position from the RIGHT end?
questions.explanation: From the right, Arjun's place is 15 + 1 − 4 = 12. So Arjun is 12th from the right.

questions.q: The pattern uses two rules again and again (+6, then −2): 7, 13, 11, 17, 15, ___?
questions.explanation: The rules take turns: add 6, then take away 2. The last move was taking away 2, so now we add 6: 15 + 6 = 21.

questions.q: Three of these numbers follow the same rule. Which number breaks the rule: 5, 10, 15, 12?
questions.explanation: 5, 10, 15 all belong to the table of 5, but 12 is not in the table of 5.

questions.q: What number comes next in the pattern: 14, 17, 20, 23, ___?
questions.explanation: The numbers grow by 3 each time: 23 + 3 = 26.

questions.q: Which small word is hiding inside the word CHAIRS?
questions.explanation: Read the letters of CHAIRS in order: the letters H-A-I-R sit together and spell HAIR.

questions.q: If A = 1, B = 2, C = 3 and so on, which word do the numbers 4, 15, 7 spell?
questions.explanation: 4 = D, 15 = O, 7 = G. So the numbers spell DOG.

questions.q: Which letter comes next: T, R, P, N, ___?
questions.explanation: The letters jump backward by 2 each time, so after N comes L.

questions.q: Clean is to dirty as Loud is to ___? (Think of opposites.)
questions.explanation: Dirty is the opposite of clean, and quiet is the opposite of loud.

faq.q: How do you solve odd one out?
faq.a: Find the property most of the group shares — shape, number type or category — and pick the one that does not share it.
A related pair is given and you complete a second pair using the same relationship, e.g. clean is to dirty as loud is to quiet.
